sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: CFO vs. Net Income Conversion: Operating cash flow converted 70% of reported net profit. Profit is running ahead of cash generation, which points to working-capital or accrual quality issues.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 72 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Earnings Volatility Check: Earnings per share fell in 1 of the last 4 years with a growth standard deviation of 39 points. Earnings are erratic, which argues for a wider margin of safety.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded 7.5% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 0 hard red flags and 4 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 65/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
